[[File:Chordal bipartite revised 2.svg|upright=0.8|thumb|Every [[cycle (graph theory)|cycle]] of length at least 6 has a chord connecting two vertices that are a distance >&nbsp;1 apart from each other in the cycle.]]

In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] area of [[graph theory]], a '''chordal bipartite graph''' is a [[bipartite graph]] ''B''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''X'',''Y'',''E'') in which every [[cycle (graph theory)|cycle]] of length at least 6 in ''B'' has a ''chord'', i.e., an edge that connects two vertices that are a distance >&nbsp;1 apart from each other in the cycle.
<ref>{{harvtxt|Golumbic|1980}}, p. 261, {{harvtxt|Brandstädt|Le|Spinrad|1999}}, Definition 3.4.1, p. 43.</ref>
A better name would be weakly chordal and bipartite since chordal bipartite graphs are in general not [[chordal]] as the induced cycle of length 4 shows.

==Characterizations==
Chordal bipartite graphs have various characterizations in terms of [[perfect elimination ordering]]s, [[hypergraph]]s and [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrices]]. They are closely related to [[strongly chordal graph]]s. 
By definition, chordal bipartite graphs have a [[Forbidden graph characterization|forbidden subgraph characterization]] as the graphs that do not contain 
any [[induced cycle]] of length 3 or of length at least 5 (so-called holes) as an [[induced subgraph]]. Thus, a graph ''G'' is chordal bipartite if and only if 
''G'' is [[triangle-free graph|triangle-free]] and hole-free. In {{harvtxt|Golumbic|1980}}, two other characterizations are mentioned: 
''B'' is chordal bipartite if and only if every minimal edge separator induces a complete bipartite subgraph in ''B'' if and only if every induced 
subgraph is perfect elimination bipartite.

Martin Farber has shown: A graph is strongly chordal if and only if the bipartite incidence graph of its clique hypergraph is chordal bipartite. 
<ref>{{harvtxt|Farber|1983}}; {{harvtxt|Brandstädt|Le|Spinrad|1999}}, Theorem 3.4.1, p. 43.</ref>

A similar characterization holds for the closed neighborhood hypergraph: A graph is strongly chordal if and only if the bipartite incidence graph of its 
closed neighborhood hypergraph is chordal bipartite.<ref>{{harvtxt|Brandstädt|1991}}</ref>

Another result found by Elias Dahlhaus is: A bipartite graph ''B''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''X'',''Y'',''E'') is chordal bipartite if and only if the [[split graph]] resulting from making ''X'' a clique is strongly chordal.<ref>{{harvtxt|Brandstädt|Le|Spinrad|1999}}, Corollary 8.3.2, p. 129.</ref>

A bipartite graph ''B''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''X'',''Y'',''E'') is chordal bipartite if and only if every induced subgraph of ''B'' has a maximum ''X''-neighborhood ordering and a 
maximum Y-neighborhood ordering.<ref>{{harvtxt|Dragan|Voloshin|1996}}</ref>

Various results describe the relationship between chordal bipartite graphs and totally balanced neighborhood hypergraphs of bipartite graphs.
<ref>{{harvtxt|Brandstädt|Le|Spinrad|1999}}, Theorems 8.2.5, 8.2.6, pp. 126–127.</ref>
 
A characterization of chordal bipartite graphs in terms of intersection graphs related to hypergraphs is given in.<ref>{{harvtxt|Huang|2006}}</ref> 
  
A bipartite graph is chordal bipartite if and only if its [[adjacency matrix]] is [[Balanced matrix|totally balanced]] if and only if the adjacency matrix is [[Gamma-free Matrix|Gamma-free]].
<ref>{{harvtxt|Farber|1983}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Chordal bipartite graphs can be recognized in time {{nowrap|O(min(''n''<sup>2</sup>, (''n'' + ''m'') log ''n''))}} for a graph with ''n'' vertices and 
''m'' edges.<ref>{{harvtxt|Lubiw|1987}}; {{harvtxt|Paige|Tarjan|1987}}; {{harvtxt|Spinrad|1993}}; {{harvtxt|Spinrad|2003}}.</ref>

==Complexity of problems==
Various problems such as Hamiltonian cycle,<ref>{{harvtxt|Müller|1996}}</ref> Steiner tree <ref>{{harvtxt|Müller|Brandstädt|1987}}</ref> and Efficient Domination 
<ref>{{harvtxt|Lu|Tang|2002}}</ref> remain NP-complete on chordal bipartite graphs.

Various other problems which can be solved efficiently for bipartite graphs can be solved more efficiently for chordal bipartite graphs as discussed in 
<ref>{{harvtxt|Spinrad|2003}}.</ref>

==Related graph classes==
Every chordal bipartite graph is a [[modular graph]]. The chordal bipartite graphs include the [[complete bipartite graph]]s and the bipartite [[distance-hereditary graph]]s.<ref>[http://www.graphclasses.org/classes/gc_79.html Chordal bipartite graphs], Information System on Graph Classes and their Inclusions, retrieved 2016-09-30.</ref>
